## Captain's intent
The quick tour is two variables, the text. You should make sure that the things are centered by the box that you created. And also the instruction on the first page is a little bit too verbal and repeated as well. To select a preloaded trajectory or click upload trajectory, though that block of text can be removed and make the quick tour description, the four step, make them much more easy to read. ## Firstmate spec

Fixes:
1. **Tour spotlight centering (steps 2–4):** The spotlight/"circled" box must vertically (and horizontally as needed) center the highlighted control(s). Today the box does not align with the content for Choose trajectory / ε-δ / Load. Fix `placeTourCard` / spotlight rect math (or CSS) so the spotlight box is centered on the target element(s). Verify at ~1280px desktop and ~390px mobile.
2. **ε and δ as the two variables:** Keep the Accuracy / ε-δ tour step about those two variables only. Short copy, max two sentences. Keep paper complexity O(ε^{-4} log(1/ε)) and Fréchet (1+ε)δ only if they still fit in two short sentences; prefer clarity over packing. No "match tolerance" / "grid spacing".
3. **Shorten all four start-tour steps** to at most two short sentences each (Welcome may keep the paper link). Easy to read; cut verbal fluff.
4. **Remove repeated start-page instruction block:** The first-page / empty-state prose that repeats "Select a preloaded trajectory or click Upload trajectory" (and similar duplicated instruction blocks under `#dropHint` / desktop-instructions) should be removed or drastically reduced so the quick tour carries that guidance instead. Do not leave two copies of the same how-to on the start screen.

After commit, run /no-mistakes through green CI and open a PR (stack on #14 if that is still open and unmerged; otherwise into main). Report full PR URL. Do not merge.

Also fix tour backdrop so spotlighted controls remain clickable (`pointer-events: none` on the tour backdrop while `.has-spotlight`) - related click-blocking of the trajectory dropdown while the tour highlights it.

1. First action: create your branch: `git checkout -b fm/tour-ux-polish`
2. Run `no-mistakes doctor`; if it reports the repo is not initialized here, run `no-mistakes init`.

# Rules
1. Never push to the default branch. Never merge a PR.
2. Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it.
3. Use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations.
4. Report status by appending one line:
   `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/Users/sinchunyeung/github/firstmate/state/tour-ux-polish.status'`
   States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed.
   Each append wakes firstmate, so report sparingly: only phase changes a supervisor
   would act on (setup done, bug reproduced, fix implemented, validation passed) and the
   needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed states. No step-by-step FYI progress lines;
   firstmate reads your pane for that.

   turn after it; continue the same stage until a defined `done:` gate under Definition of done.
   Use `paused: {why}` - distinct from `blocked:` - ONLY when you are deliberately idling on a
   known external wait you expect to clear on its own (an upstream release, a rate-limit reset,

   cadence instead of treating it as a possible wedge. Use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need help.

   Firstmate's reply normally writes that closing line at answer time; when a blocker or wait clears WITHOUT a firstmate reply, append `resolved: {how it cleared}` yourself (same `[key=<slug>]` if you opened it with one) as you resume.

# Definition of done
Delivery contract: mode=no-mistakes

When you believe it is complete, append `done: {summary}` to the status file and stop.

  It auto-resolves every gate including ask-user findings with no escalation, and answering your own ask-user finding is a hard rule violation.

After /no-mistakes reports CI green (the CI-ready return point - do not wait for it to keep monitoring in the background until merge), append `done: PR {url} checks green` and stop. You are finished.

Backdrop uses `pointer-events: none` while `.has-spotlight`. Start tour copy is ≤2 short sentences per step (ε/δ only on step 3). Drop-hint prose and desktop Instructions list removed; mobile start help is tips-only.
